# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| README.md | Setup, supported runtime/provider, exact intake/test/accuracy-check commands, environment-variable names, and how to inspect the queue |
| Source code and dependency lockfile | Runnable application, extraction prompt, schema and model request configuration |
| deliverables/extractions.jsonl | One current record per message: document_id, source_sha256, extraction (schema-conforming object, or null on error), status, owner, next_action, error (null on success), and response_source (`mock`, or the provider and model ID that produced the record) |
| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |
| deliverables/accuracy.md | Source-derived expected fields for the 20 supplied messages and one paraphrase you author; the field-comparison procedure, exact-match counting/denominator rules, factual-error reporting and model/configuration; distinguish mocked examples from any optional live observations |
| deliverables/request-evidence.json | Credential-redacted example model request showing the model ID and configuration used, plus the implemented response handling |
| deliverables/verification.md | Verification commands and assertions, their intended comparisons, operating limits, and any observed results or repairs clearly identified as such |
| Coding-session capture | Session record paired with the submitted commit, collected through the facilitator's capture setup |

## Submission
Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. Use mocked responses for reproducible development examples, and label each recorded observation with its configuration and whether it used a mock or provider response. The committed deliverables may come from mocked or provider responses; each record's response_source says which.
# Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. def verify_artifacts(root):
    root = Path(root).resolve()

    generation = (deliverables / "current").resolve(strict=True)
    if generation.parent != deliverables / "generations":
        raise ValueError("Current generation is outside the deliverables snapshot directory")
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in (generation / "extractions.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]

    expected_path = deliverables / "expected-fields.json"
    rules_path = deliverables / "accuracy-rules.json"
    expected = json.loads(expected_path.read_text())["records"]
    rules = json.loads(rules_path.read_text())
    paths = sorted((root / "materials/requests").glob("*.json")) + [root / "materials/paraphrases/IT-021.json"]
    documents = {path.name: read_export(path) for path in paths}
    score = score_records(records, expected, documents, rules)
    errors = []
    if (score["factual_errors"] or score["routing_errors"] or score["evidence_errors"]
            or score["unexpected_documents"]):
        errors.append("Current records differ from source-grounded expectations")
    by_document = {record["document_id"]: record for record in records}
    if len(queue) != len(records) or len({r["document_id"] for r in queue}) != len(records):
        errors.append("Queue document identities are not unique and complete")
    for item in queue:
        record = by_document.get(item["document_id"], {})
        for field in ("attempt_id", "source_sha256", "generation_id", "status", "owner", "next_action", "error"):
            if item.get(field) != record.get(field):
                errors.append(f"Queue/extraction mismatch: {item['document_id']} {field}")
        if item.get("generation_id") != generation.name:
            errors.append("Generation identity does not match the pinned snapshot")
    historical = {(record["document_id"], record["attempt_id"], record["source_sha256"]) for record in history}
    for record in records:
        if (record["document_id"], record["attempt_id"], record["source_sha256"]) not in historical:
            errors.append(f"Missing current attempt in history: {record['document_id']}")
        for key, path in (("prompt_sha256", root / "src/extraction_prompt.txt"),
                          ("schema_sha256", root / "snapshot.schema.json"),
                          ("policy_sha256", root / "materials/office-policy.md"),
                          ("routing_sha256", root / "src/review.py")):
            if record["processing_settings"].get(key) != hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest():
                errors.append(f"Processing provenance differs: {record['document_id']} {key}")
    evidence = json.loads((deliverables / "request-evidence.json").read_text())
    # Construct the implemented request without loading a credential or making a call.
    transport = type("MockTransportIdentity", (), {"response_source": "mock"})()
    provider = AnthropicProvider(transport=transport)
    actual = provider.request_evidence(documents["IT-001.json"])
    for field, value in actual.items():
        if evidence.get(field) != value:
            errors.append(f"Request evidence differs from implemented adapter: {field}")
    if evidence.get("headers", {}).get("Authorization") != "[REDACTED]":
        errors.append("Request credential header is not redacted")
    accuracy = (deliverables / "accuracy.md").read_text()
    for path in (expected_path, rules_path):
        if hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() not in accuracy:
            errors.append("Accuracy report does not identify the frozen artifact hashes")
    verification = (deliverables / "verification.md").read_text()
    for required in ("Observed", "Intended", "C1", "C2", "C3", "mock", "2,000", "interruption"):
        if required not in verification:
            errors.append(f"Verification documentation missing {required}")
    return {"passed": not errors, "documents": len(records), "scalar_matches": score["matched"],
            "response_sources": score["response_sources"], "errors": errors}

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd())

    result = verify_artifacts(args.root)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    return int(not result["passed"])

# Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3
import uuid

from .exports import SourceDocument
from .review import intake


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def processing_settings(provider):
    def digest(path):
        return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    return {
        "provider": provider.provenance() if hasattr(provider, "provenance") else {"provider": "mock"},
        "response_source": getattr(provider, "response_source", "mock"),
        "prompt_sha256": digest(getattr(provider, "prompt_path", ROOT / "src/extraction_prompt.txt")),
        "schema_sha256": digest(getattr(provider, "schema_path", ROOT / "snapshot.schema.json")),
        "policy_sha256": digest(getattr(provider, "policy_path", ROOT / "materials/office-policy.md")),
        "routing_sha256": digest(ROOT / "src/review.py"),
    }


class FileLock:
    def __init__(self, path, *, blocking=False):
        self.handle = Path(path).open("a+b")
        try:
            fcntl.flock(self.handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX | (0 if blocking else fcntl.LOCK_NB))
        except BaseException:
            self.handle.close()
            raise

    def close(self):
        if not self.handle.closed:
            fcntl.flock(self.handle, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            self.handle.close()


@dataclass
class Attempt:
    attempt_id: int
    token: str
    document: SourceDocument
    settings: dict
    record: dict
    reused: bool = False
    lock: FileLock | None = None

    def close(self):
        if self.lock:
            self.lock.close()


class Store:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = Path(path).resolve()
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.locks = self.path.with_suffix(self.path.suffix + ".locks")
        self.locks.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
            db.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attempts (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, token TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                document_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, raw BLOB NOT NULL,
                settings TEXT NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL, result TEXT NOT NULL)""")
            db.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS by_document ON attempts(document_id, id)")

    @contextmanager
    def connection(self):
        db = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
        db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()

    def begin(self, document, settings, *, retry=False):
        token = uuid.uuid4().hex
        lock = FileLock(self.locks / token)
        encoded = json.dumps(settings, sort_keys=True)
        try:
            with self.connection() as db:
                db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
                previous = db.execute("SELECT * FROM attempts WHERE document_id=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",
                                      (document.document_id,)).fetchone()
                if (not retry and previous and previous["source_sha256"] == document.source_sha256
                        and previous["settings"] == encoded):
                    db.commit()
                    lock.close()
                    return Attempt(previous["id"], previous["token"], document, settings,
                                   json.loads(previous["result"]), reused=True)
                record = {
                    "document_id": document.document_id, "source_sha256": document.source_sha256,
                    "status": "pending", "owner": "IT Service Desk", "next_action": "resume-extraction",
                    "extraction": None, "error": None, "response_source": settings["response_source"],
                    "processing_settings": settings,
                }
                cursor = db.execute("""INSERT INTO attempts
                    (token, document_id, source_sha256, raw, settings, state, result)
                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'pending', ?)""",
                    (token, document.document_id, document.source_sha256, document.raw_bytes, encoded, "{}"))
                record["attempt_id"] = cursor.lastrowid
                db.execute("UPDATE attempts SET result=? WHERE id=?", (json.dumps(record), cursor.lastrowid))
                db.commit()
                return Attempt(cursor.lastrowid, token, document, settings, record, lock=lock)
        except BaseException:
            lock.close()
            raise

    def complete(self, attempt, result):
        if attempt.reused or attempt.lock is None:
            raise ValueError("Only the owning attempt can publish completion")
        if (result["document_id"] != attempt.document.document_id
                or result["source_sha256"] != attempt.document.source_sha256):
            raise ValueError("Completion source does not match its attempt")
        record = dict(result, attempt_id=attempt.attempt_id, processing_settings=attempt.settings)
        try:
            with self.connection() as db:
                db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
                cursor = db.execute("UPDATE attempts SET state='completed', result=? WHERE id=? AND token=? AND state='pending'",
                                    (json.dumps(record), attempt.attempt_id, attempt.token))
                if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                    raise ValueError("Attempt has already completed")
                db.commit()
            return record
        finally:
            attempt.close()

    def process(self, document, provider, *, retry=False):
        attempt = self.begin(document, processing_settings(provider), retry=retry)
        if attempt.reused:
            return attempt.record
        try:
            result, = intake([document], provider)
            return self.complete(attempt, result)
        finally:
            attempt.close()

    def current(self):
        with self.connection() as db:
            return self._current(db)

    @staticmethod
    def _current(db):
        return [json.loads(row[0]) for row in db.execute("""SELECT result FROM attempts
            WHERE id IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM attempts GROUP BY document_id) ORDER BY document_id""")]

    def history(self, document_id=None):
        with self.connection() as db:
            if document_id is None:
                rows = db.execute("SELECT result FROM attempts ORDER BY id")
            else:
                rows = db.execute("SELECT result FROM attempts WHERE document_id=? ORDER BY id", (document_id,))
            return [json.loads(row[0]) for row in rows]

    def pending(self):
        with self.connection() as db:
            return [json.loads(row[0]) for row in db.execute("SELECT result FROM attempts WHERE state='pending' ORDER BY id")]

    def claim(self, attempt_id):
        with self.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM attempts WHERE id=? AND state='pending'", (attempt_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        try:
            lock = FileLock(self.locks / row["token"])
        except BlockingIOError:
            return None
        # Recheck after locking: another resumer may have completed since the read.
        with self.connection() as db:
            if db.execute("SELECT state FROM attempts WHERE id=?", (attempt_id,)).fetchone()[0] != "pending":
                lock.close()
                return None
        raw = row["raw"]
        source = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        document = SourceDocument(row["document_id"], raw, row["source_sha256"], source["message"],
                                  {k: v for k, v in source.items() if k != "message"})
        return Attempt(row["id"], row["token"], document, json.loads(row["settings"]),
                       json.loads(row["result"]), lock=lock)

    def export(self, destination, *, fault=None):
        destination = Path(destination).resolve()
        destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        lock = FileLock(destination / ".publication.lock", blocking=True)
        try:
            with self.connection() as db:
                db.execute("BEGIN")
                records = self._current(db)
                history = [json.loads(r[0]) for r in db.execute("SELECT result FROM attempts ORDER BY id")]
                db.commit()
            generation_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
            generation = destination / "generations" / generation_id
            generation.mkdir(parents=True)
            records = [dict(record, generation_id=generation_id) for record in records]
            self._write(generation / "extractions.jsonl", "".join(json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for r in records))
            if fault:
                fault("after_extractions")
            queue = [{k: r[k] for k in ("document_id", "attempt_id", "source_sha256", "generation_id",
                                       "status", "owner", "next_action", "error")} for r in records]
            self._write(generation / "queue.json", json.dumps(queue, indent=2) + "\n")
            self._write(generation / "history.jsonl", "".join(json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for r in history))
            self._sync_directory(generation)
            self._sync_directory(generation.parent)
            for name in ("queue.json", "extractions.jsonl", "history.jsonl"):
                link = destination / name
                if not os.path.lexists(link):
                    link.symlink_to(Path("current") / name)
            temporary = destination / f".current-{generation_id}"
            temporary.symlink_to(Path("generations") / generation_id, target_is_directory=True)
            os.replace(temporary, destination / "current")
            self._sync_directory(destination)
            return generation
        finally:
            lock.close()

    @staticmethod
    def _write(path, text):
        with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(text)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())

    @staticmethod
    def _sync_directory(path):
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
        try:
            os.fsync(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

FAKE_SECRET = "REDACTED"


def saved(name):
    return json.loads((MOCKS / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


class SavedHTTPTransport:
    response_source = "mock"

    def __init__(self, fixtures):
        self.fixtures = iter(fixtures)
        self.calls = []

    def __call__(self, *, method, url, headers, body, timeout):
        self.calls.append(deepcopy({"method": method, "url": url, "headers": headers,
                                    "body": body, "timeout": timeout}))
        scenario = next(self.fixtures)
        if isinstance(scenario, str):
            return SimpleNamespace(status_code=200, headers={},
                                   body=json.dumps(saved(scenario)).encode("utf-8"))
        if "exception" in scenario:
            kind = {"TimeoutError": TimeoutError, "InterruptedError": InterruptedError}
            raise kind[scenario["exception"]](scenario["message"].format(fake_secret=REDACTED
        text = json.dumps(scenario["body"]).replace("{fake_secret}", FAKE_SECRET)
        return SimpleNamespace(status_code=scenario["status_code"],
                               headers=scenario.get("headers", {}), body=text.encode("utf-8"))


class ProviderBoundaryContract(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.network = mock.Mock(side_effect=AssertionError("network access forbidden"))
        for patcher in (
            mock.patch.object(socket, "socket", self.network),
            mock.patch.object(socket, "create_connection", self.network),
            mock.patch.object(os, "environ", NoCredentials()),
        ):
            patcher.start()
            self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        from src.exports import read_export
        from src.provider import ProviderConfig, AnthropicProvider
        from src.processing import process_batch

        self.config_class = ProviderConfig
        self.provider_class = AnthropicProvider
        self.process_batch = process_batch
        self.documents = [read_export(ROOT / f"materials/requests/IT-{n:03d}.json")
                          for n in (1, 2)]
        self.router = mock.Mock(return_value={"status": "validated", "owner": "routing-spy",
                                            "next_action": "inspect"})
        self.logs = io.StringIO()
        handler = logging.StreamHandler(self.logs)
        logger = logging.getLogger("src")
        logger.addHandler(handler)
        self.addCleanup(logger.removeHandler, handler)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.network.assert_not_called()

    def provider(self, fixtures, **settings):
        self.transport = SavedHTTPTransport(fixtures)
        # Inject a fake credential loader; never read the real API_KEY environment.
        return self.provider_class(self.config_class(**settings), transport=self.transport,
                                   credential_loader=mock.Mock(return_value=FAKE_SECRET))

    def run_batch(self, provider, documents=None):

                                  provider, self.router)

        self.assertEqual(result["response_source"], "mock")
        self.assertEqual(result["provider_config"]["model"], "claude-sonnet-5-5")
        self.assertNotIn(FAKE_SECRET, json.dumps(result) + self.logs.getvalue())

    def test_T04_supported_request_and_source_grounded_candidate(self):

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProviderConfig:
    endpoint: str = "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages"
    model: str = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
    max_tokens: int = 8192
    timeout: float = 60
    api_version: str = "2026-10-21"


class ProviderFailure(Exception):
    def __init__(self, kind, detail, retry_after_seconds=None):
        super().__init__(detail)
        self.kind = kind
        self.retry_after_seconds = retry_after_seconds


def http_transport(*, method, url, headers, body, timeout):
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8"),
                                     headers=headers, method=method)
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        response = exc
    with response:
        return SimpleNamespace(status_code=response.code, headers=dict(response.headers),
                               body=response.read())


def environment_credential():
    return os.environ["API_KEY"]


class AnthropicProvider:
    def __init__(self, config=None, *, transport=http_transport,
                 credential_loader=environment_credential, prompt_path=None,
                 schema_path=None, policy_path=None):
        self.config = config or ProviderConfig()
        self.transport = transport
        self.credential_loader = credential_loader
        self.prompt_path = Path(prompt_path or ROOT / "src/extraction_prompt.txt")
        self.schema_path = Path(schema_path or ROOT / "snapshot.schema.json")
        self.policy_path = Path(policy_path or ROOT / "materials/office-policy.md")
        self.response_source = getattr(transport, "response_source", f"anthropic/{self.config.model}")

    def provenance(self):
        return asdict(self.config)

    def _body(self, document_id, message):
        return {
            "model": self.config.model, "max_tokens": self.config.max_tokens, "stream": False,
            "system": self.prompt_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(
                {"document_id": document_id, "message": message})}]}],
            "output_config": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": json.loads(
                self.schema_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}},
        }

    def request_evidence(self, document):
        # Construct redacted evidence without loading any credential.
        return {
            "method": "POST", "url": self.config.endpoint,
            "headers": {"Authorization": "[REDACTED]", "Content-Type": "application/json",
                        "anthropic-version": self.config.api_version},
            "body": self._body(document.document_id, document.message),
            "response_source": self.response_source,
            "response_handling": ["http-status", "refusal", "completion", "parse", "schema", "quotes", "routing"],
        }

    def extract(self, document_id, message):
        try:
            credential = self.credential_loader()
        except (KeyError, ValueError):
            raise ProviderFailure("configuration", "Set API_KEY before provider intake") from None
        if not credential:
            raise ProviderFailure("configuration", "Set API_KEY before provider intake")
        try:
            response = self.transport(
                method="POST", url=self.config.endpoint, timeout=self.config.timeout,
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {credential}", "Content-Type": "application/json",
                         "anthropic-version": self.config.api_version},
                body=self._body(document_id, message),
            )
        except TimeoutError:
            raise ProviderFailure("timeout", "Provider timed out") from None
        except InterruptedError:
            raise ProviderFailure("interrupted", "Provider request interrupted") from None
        except (OSError, urllib.error.URLError):
            raise ProviderFailure("unavailable", "Provider connection unavailable") from None
        if response.status_code == 429:
            headers = {key.lower(): value for key, value in response.headers.items()}
            try:
                retry_after = max(0, float(headers.get("retry-after", 0)))
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                retry_after = None
            raise ProviderFailure("rate_limit", "Provider rate limited the request", retry_after)
        if response.status_code != 200:
            raise ProviderFailure("unavailable", f"Provider HTTP status {response.status_code}")
        try:
            envelope = json.loads(response.body)
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
            raise ProviderFailure("parse", "Provider returned invalid response JSON") from None
        if not isinstance(envelope, dict):
            raise ProviderFailure("completion", "Provider response is not a message object")
        if envelope.get("stop_reason") == "refusal":
            raise ProviderFailure("refusal", "Provider declined extraction")
        if (envelope.get("type") != "message" or envelope.get("role") != "assistant"
                or envelope.get("stop_reason") != "end_turn"):
            raise ProviderFailure("completion", "Provider response did not complete normally")
        blocks = envelope.get("content")
        if (not isinstance(blocks, list) or not blocks
                or any(not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "text"
                       or not isinstance(block.get("text"), str) for block in blocks)):
            raise ProviderFailure("completion", "Provider response has invalid content blocks")
        return {"status": "completed", "refusal": None,
                "output_text": "".join(block["text"] for block in blocks),
                "response_source": self.response_source}
